title: MACH Factory Runner Policy v2
description: The machine-local authorization for unattended execution: .factory/local/runner.json. Written by a person's pull the first time it hands work to the supervisor on this machine (enabled_by "pull"), or by factory enable, in one step. Git-ignored, readable only by its owner, and valid only on the machine and in the folder where it was written. Absent, unreadable or invalid means disabled; enabled false is a person's factory disable, which a pull never undoes. Project settings may restrict what it grants and can never widen it.

autonomy.description: observe: discover, take in and plan; start no agent. supervised: also run eligible work, stopping at every human gate.

auto_sync.description: Fetch from the shared repository on a timer. Never changes a checkout.

allow_merge.description: False (factory enable --no-merge): every execution stops before the merge station. True, the default: the project's own merge settings decide.

persistent.description: A per-user service keeps the supervisor running.

max_risk.description: Tickets above this tier wait for a person.

limits.description: max_parallel, max_runs_per_day and both budgets are optional: absent or null means no limit of this machine's own (the project's factory.* settings may still set one; for max_parallel the project's own ceiling governs). With no per-run budget, no --max-budget-usd is passed to Claude.

allowed_tools.description: The only tools an execution may use. A bare 'Bash' is never valid.

excluded_slices.description: Slices left to the engineer. Always empty when written now; an older authorization may list work that was here when it was enabled.

claude.description: The Claude Code program found at activation.

enabled_by.description: "pull" when a pull wrote it; otherwise the person who ran factory enable.

execution_risk_accepted.description: Written by versions before M23: a person's acceptance of the execution risk for one tool list. No longer written or required; a file that has it still reads.

monitoring_requests.description: M8 D7. Optional; missing reads as false. True only when an engineer enabled supervised autonomy with --monitoring-requests: the supervisor may take in and run issues filed by the project's monitoring accounts. Ignored in observe autonomy; the project setting factory.monitoring_requests false forbids it, and no project setting grants it.
